questions.text: Platform Operating License: Legal right to operate: (1) Transport platform license (if required); (2) Compliance with local transport regulations; (3) Route permits (for specific areas); (4) Cooperation with transport authority; (5) Reporting obligations (trip data, safety incidents); (6) Tax compliance (VAT, withholding); (7) Renewal and audit processes.
questions.evidence_required: Operating license, Regulatory filings, Tax compliance certificates
questions.africa_specific_notes: Many platforms operate in regulatory grey zones. Governments scrambling to regulate (e.g., Kenya's Uber regulations).

questions.text: Driver & Vehicle Licensing Compliance: Individual compliance: (1) Driver license verification (PSV/commercial); (2) Vehicle registration verification; (3) Insurance verification (comprehensive, third-party); (4) Roadworthiness certificate; (5) Route permit (for commercial vehicles); (6) Periodic re-verification; (7) Suspension for non-compliance.
questions.evidence_required: Verification logs, Compliance dashboard, Suspension records
questions.africa_specific_notes: PSV (Public Service Vehicle) license required for commercial transport. Many drivers use private car insurance (illegal).

questions.text: Passenger Insurance Coverage: Protection for riders: (1) Mandatory passenger insurance; (2) Coverage limits (death, injury); (3) Claims process clarity; (4) Response time for claims; (5) Transparency on coverage gaps; (6) Third-party liability; (7) Coverage during 'offline' trips (cash).
questions.evidence_required: Insurance policy, Claims process documentation, Settlement stats
questions.africa_specific_notes: Insurance penetration low. Platforms often provide blanket cover. Claims process slow and opaque.

questions.text: Driver & Goods Insurance: Protection for drivers/cargo: (1) Driver injury/death cover; (2) Vehicle damage cover; (3) Goods-in-transit insurance (delivery); (4) Liability for lost/damaged goods; (5) Coverage during platform vs offline work; (6) Premium subsidy (if any); (7) Claims support.
questions.evidence_required: Driver insurance policy, Goods insurance policy, Claims logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Drivers often uninsured (can't afford). Goods insurance rare. Disputes over lost packages common.

questions.text: Driver Classification & Rights: Employee vs contractor: (1) Legal classification (employee, contractor, partner); (2) Right to organize (unions); (3) Minimum earnings guarantee; (4) Working hours limits (fatigue management); (5) Rest period enforcement; (6) Grievance mechanism; (7) Protection from arbitrary deactivation.
questions.evidence_required: Employment contracts, Union recognition agreements, Grievance logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Gig economy classification is contested. Drivers often work 12+ hour days. Deactivation without appeal is common.

questions.text: Health & Safety Protections: Protecting drivers: (1) PPE provision (helmets for boda-boda); (2) Safety training (defensive driving); (3) Accident support (medical, legal); (4) Mental health support (stress, trauma); (5) COVID-19 protocols (sanitizer, masks); (6) Harassment reporting (by passengers); (7) Security features (panic button).
questions.evidence_required: Safety training logs, PPE distribution records, Incident support cases
questions.africa_specific_notes: Boda-boda riders face high accident risk. Harassment of drivers (especially women) is common. Mental health support rare.

questions.text: Anti-Fraud Measures: Preventing scams: (1) Fake driver detection (account sharing); (2) Fake trip detection (GPS spoofing); (3) Payment fraud prevention (stolen cards); (4) Promo code abuse prevention; (5) Collusion detection (driver-passenger); (6) Merchant fraud (fake orders); (7) Whistleblower protection.
questions.evidence_required: Fraud detection algorithms, Investigation logs, Deactivation stats
questions.africa_specific_notes: GPS spoofing (fake trips) is rampant. Account sharing common (drivers rent accounts). Promo code abuse is a major loss.

questions.text: Passenger & Driver Safety Governance: Preventing harm: (1) Background check policy (criminal, driving); (2) Real-time monitoring (SOS alerts); (3) Incident response team (24/7); (4) Collaboration with police; (5) Driver suspension for safety violations; (6) Passenger blacklist (for harassment); (7) Safety audit frequency.
questions.evidence_required: Safety policy, Incident response logs, Police collaboration MOUs
questions.africa_specific_notes: High-profile assaults/kidnappings damage trust. Real-time monitoring and police collaboration are essential.

scoring_notes: Layer 3 (Governance) for Transport in SSA: Regulatory compliance (licensing, insurance) is often weak. Driver welfare (gig economy rights) is a growing issue. Safety governance is the top public concern.
